newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory 96/97 cocoa farm prices mid-October-minister.
newsitem.headline: Ivory 96/97 cocoa farm prices mid-October-minister.

text.p: Ivory Coast will announce its 1996/97 cocoa farm-gate prices around mid-October, Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze told Reuters on Thursday.
"We will announce that around the middle of October," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

On Wednesday, Agriculture Minister Lambert Kouassi Konan announced an October 15 date for the start of the new cocoa marketing season at a review of the 1995/96 cocoa and coffee season in the commercial capital Abidjan.
Exporters and buyers in Ivory Coast say they expect little or no change to the recommended minimum farm-gate cocoa price, currently 320 CFA francs per kilo.

"The information I have from the Caistab is that they do not want to change the price," said a source, declining to be named. "There is no reason to change the price as (the result will be that) there will be more cocoa. That is not what they want."
Kouassi Konan also said that the 1996/97 coffee marketing season would begin either at the end of 1996 or early in 1997, much later than in previous years.
Exporters and buyers expect a decrease in the price for coffee, when those prices are eventually announced.
